newsitem.title: CANADA: Manitoba harvest advances, frost damage minimal.
newsitem.headline: Manitoba harvest advances, frost damage minimal.

text.p: Manitoba's harvest advanced rapidly on good weekend weather after rain delays the previous week while frost damage was minimal, Manitoba Agriculture's report for the week ended September 16 said.

Southwest Manitoba - Seventy-five to 80 percent of cereals were harvested with yields seen at or above average. Fusarium and ergot in wheat don't seem to be major downgrading factors. Half of canola was combined as was 25 percent of flax.
Northwest Manitoba - Thirty percent of crops were combined with 75 percent swathed. Wheat yields averaged 35 bushels an acre with good protein levels. Barley yield as 50 to 60 bu/ac.
Canola yield was 25 bushels an acre. Minimal frost damage occured.

Central Manitoba - More than 50 percent of cereals, canola were combined. Yields ranged 30-40 bu/ac. Grades and quality of cereals in the Red River Valley were better than expected. Fifty percent of flax was harvested, yielding 25 bu/ac.

Eastern Manitoba - Cereals were 75 to 80 percent combined. Rain caused some downgrading of wheat due to bleaching. Test weights were generally good except for oats that lodged early. Protein levels of wheat were average. Canola was 90 percent swathed with combining started, yields seen at 30 to 35 bu/ac.

Interlake region - Sixty-five percent of wheat, barley were combined, 40 percent of canola was combined and 15 percent of flax was combined. Yields were above average. Grades were reduced somewhat on poor weather earlier this month. Some light frost was reported on the weekend but little damage was expected.
